title: Data Staging
overview: Triage an archive audit record when an unusual actor stages multiple sensitive files together.
prerequisites: Be comfortable reading timestamps and linux audit projection fields.

attack.name: Archive via Utility
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: A large archive of sensitive files written to a shared staging area should be compared with authorized workflows.
evidence: Review input classification, output location and actor, then pivot to transfer telemetry.
false_positive: An authorized support bundle or export can build a temporary archive.
tuning: Correlate staging paths and approval metadata. Use baselines for file count and data class.
response: Identify who owns the archive, confirm its destination and preserve evidence before deleting any temporary copies.
prevention: Limit staging access, use DLP and monitor outbound transfers from systems with sensitive datasets.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: An archive observation does not show that a transfer occurred. No files are bundled or archived by the lab.

questions.explanation: Data class and destination describe sensitivity and who could access it.

questions.prompt: Which follow-up distinguishes staging from export?
options: Another archive with the same extension
A corresponding transfer or delivery event
questions.explanation: Transfer evidence confirms movement beyond the staging location.
